items.given: An island reported once, perhaps a bank of cloud on a far edge, was copied for hundreds of years.

body.text: Early maps of the world were drawn from reports carried home by sailors and traders.
A coast that sailors had seen clearly was drawn well, while the land behind it was a guess.
Open space, however, was rarely left open, since an empty sheet looked like a failure of knowledge.
Mapmakers filled it with mountains, rivers and creatures that no one had ever met.
Some errors were stranger than that, because a copied map could invent land out of nothing.

explanation.text: 주어진 문장은 있지도 않은 섬이 수백 년 동안 베껴졌다는 이야기이므로, a copied map could invent land out of nothing 이라는 일반 진술의 실례에 해당한다. 그 진술이 놓인 자리가 ⑤ 앞 문장이니 답은 ⑤ 다. ①~④ 는 해안은 잘 그리고 그 너머는 짐작으로 채웠다는 빈칸 메우기 이야기라, 베껴 그리다 없던 땅이 생긴다는 다른 갈래가 아직 열리지 않았다. 특히 ④ 에 넣으면 Some errors were stranger than that 의 that 이 받을 앞말이 사라져 비교가 무너진다.

But is there still hope? Yes! Around the world—from local towns and villages to scientists and politicians—people are working hard to help the ocean heal. We looked at more than 200 happy-ending stories from all around the globe, where things got better for many different species. For example, in some areas, there are now more animals and plants living in the ocean than there were in years past, or species that had completely disappeared from a region “returned home” as the waters became cleaner. These success stories show that there is hope for the ocean to bounce back—with a little help from all of us.

explanation.text: "We looked at more than 200 happy-ending stories" 를 살펴 "there is hope for the ocean to bounce back" 라 맺는다. 회복의 증거가 요지다. ①·②·⑤는 피해 쪽 소재만 남기고 결론을 반대로 돌렸고 — 특히 ⑤는 200건이 **성공** 사례라는 사실을 뒤집었다 — ③은 본문에 없는 방법론이다.

insects would certainly live much longer without any fungi
the microscope has now revealed everything about these fungi
the species we cannot even see still matter and need protecting
the smallest living things are the easiest ones for us to study

explanation.text: 글은 라불이 "microscopic" 이고 "even scientists do not fully understand them yet" 이라 해 놓고 마지막 문장에서 그 사실을 교훈으로 바꾼다. 보이지 않아도 중요하다는 방향을 담은 것은 ④다. ③·⑤ 는 글이 말한 것과 정반대다 — 아직 다 알지 못한다. ①·② 는 글에 없는 비약이다.

An ice age is a period of reduced temperatures causing ice to cover large areas of the northern and southern parts of the world. A group of scientists studied changes in the shape of the Earth’s orbit around the sun, the tilt of the Earth’s axis and the movement of the axis itself, called a wobble. These three motions are believed to happen in cycles. The Serbian scientist Milutin Milankovitch developed a theory about 100 years ago that these cycles affected Earth’s long-term climate. The team noted that small changes in Earth’s orbit around the Sun caused predictable cycles of warming and cooling over a period of about 100,000 years.

items.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.passage: Mathematics is possible under conditions which are not allowed to metaphysics. All human knowledge is either experience or mathematics. A judgment is synthetic--that is to say, it co-ordinates various ideas. It is a priori--that is to say, this co-ordination is universally true and necessary, and is arrived at, not by sensual experience, but by pure reason. If there are such things as a priori judgments, then reason must be able to co-ordinate: co-ordination is a form. Reason must _possess a formative faculty._ Judging is our oldest faith; it is our habit of believing this to be true or false, of asserting or denying, our certainty that something is thus and not otherwise, our belief that we really "know"--what is believed to be true in all judgments? What are attributes?--We did not regard changes in ourselves merely as such, but as "things in themselves," which are strange to us, and which we only "perceive"; and we did not class them as phenomena, but as Being, as "attributes"; and in addition we invented a creature to which they attach themselves--that is to say, we made the effect the working cause, and the latter we made Being.
choices: 수학에 허용된 조건을 형이상학에도 그대로 허용해야 한다.
선험적 판단은 감각의 경험에서 끌어내야 한다.
사람의 앎은 경험과 수학 밖에서 찾아야 한다.
우리 안의 변화를 사물 자체로 놓고 설명해야 한다.
참이라 믿어 온 판단의 습관을 의심해 보아야 한다.

explanation.text: ⑤가 필자가 미는 바다. 글은 Judging is our oldest faith; it is our habit of believing this to be true or false 라며 판단을 믿음의 습관으로 되돌려 놓고, 그 습관이 we made the effect the working cause 라는 뒤집힘을 낳았다고 짚는다. 나머지는 글이 부정한 쪽이다 — ①은 Mathematics is possible under conditions which are not allowed to metaphysics 와 반대이고, ②는 선험이 not by sensual experience 라는 정의와 어긋난다. ③은 앎이 경험 아니면 수학이라는 서술과, ④는 필자가 지어낸 것이라 비판한 대목과 어긋나는 오답이다.

items.passage: Hurricane response crews from the U.S. Geological Survey have installed storm-tide sensors at key locations along the northeast shores of Puerto Rico in advance of Hurricane Irma. Under a mission assignment from the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the USGS deployed nine sensors. These storm-tide sensors, housed in vented steel pipes a few inches wide and about a foot long, were installed on bridges, piers, and other structures that have a good chance of surviving a storm surge during a hurricane. The information they collect will help define the depth and duration of a storm-surge, as well as the time of its arrival and retreat. As the storm approaches and passes the island, information on the storm-tide sensor deployment and the incoming data will be available on the USGS “Flood Event Viewer” at http://water.usgs.gov/floods/FEV/. Storm-surges are increases in ocean water levels generated at sea by extreme storms and can have devastating coastal impacts.

items.passage: In new research, astronomers describe how more than 200 known exoplanets are likely much larger than previously thought. It’s a finding that could change which distant worlds researchers consider potential harbors for extraterrestrial life. “We found that hundreds of exoplanets are larger than they appear, and that shifts our understanding of exoplanets on a large scale,” says Te Han, a doctoral student at University of California, Irvine and lead author of the new Astrophysical Journal Letters study. “This means we may have actually found fewer Earth-like planets so far than we thought.” Astronomers can’t observe exoplanets directly. They have to wait for a planet to pass in front of its host star, and then they measure the very subtle drop in light emanating from a star. “We’re basically measuring the shadow of the planet,” says Paul Robertson, UC Irvine professor of astronomy and study coauthor. Han’s team studied observations of hundreds of exoplanets observed by NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, and they found that light from neighboring stars can “contaminate” the light of a star an astronomer is studying.

the problem of stray light coming from neighboring stars

items.stem: 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
items.passage:
Nell lost the leather case on the last bus and did not notice until her stop. Inside it lay the flute her mother had played, worn smooth at the mouthpiece. She ran back along the lane, but the tail lights had already turned the corner. Ivo was locking the shop on that corner and caught her blank stare. He asked her what she had lost, and she could barely shape the answer. Her hands were shaking, and a bitter wind off the awning made it worse.

That night Ivo wrote the bus number on a receipt and pushed it into his coat. Nell went to the depot in the morning and found the lost property window shut. She waited on a bench until noon, watching each bus crawl in and stall. Nobody had handed in a leather case, and the clerk told her this gently. She walked home the long way, past his shop, with a lonely, steady step. He saw her pass and did not call out, because he had already begun.

The next afternoon Ivo rode the whole route from end to end. He asked each driver about a case with a brass hook on the strap. On the second run a driver remembered a woman who had carried one off. Ivo found her three streets away, sweeping the step of a narrow house. She had meant to bring it back, but shame had fixed her in place. He took the case, thanked her, and said nothing about the delay.

Two evenings later Nell opened her door and found the case on the step. There was no note, no name, and no request of any kind. She carried it in and sat with it on her knees, uncertain what to feel. The next week she played again in the front room, with the window open a crack. Ivo heard the thin sound from the corner and kept walking with a private smile. He never told her, and she never asked, and the music went on.
choices: She ran back along the lane
She waited on a bench until noon
She walked home the long way
She had meant to bring it back
The next week she played again

explanation.text: (d) 의 She 는 Nell 이 아니라 가방을 가져간 여자다. 바로 앞에 'a driver remembered a woman who had carried one off' 와 'Ivo found her three streets away, sweeping the step of a narrow house' 가 놓여 있고, 뒤이어 'shame had fixed her in place' 로 같은 인물이 이어진다. 나머지 넷의 She/she 는 모두 Nell 이다 — (a) 는 버스를 놓치고 골목을 되짚어 뛴 Nell, (b) 와 (c) 는 차고지에서 정오까지 기다리다 먼 길로 돌아온 Nell, (e) 는 창을 조금 열고 다시 플루트를 분 Nell 이다.

items.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.passage: Previous work has demonstrated that New Zealanders who do not speak Māori but are regularly exposed to the language develop implicit knowledge of it. The core of this knowledge, it has been argued, is the ‘proto-lexicon’—a set of stored word-forms, without associated meaning, which yields subsequent Māori phonotactic and morphological knowledge. Previous research shows that having a proto-lexicon gives learners a head start in learning Māori word meanings in formal education. We investigate experimentally whether the proto-lexicon confers an advantage for attaching meanings to words. In Experiment 1, non-Māori-speaking New Zealanders were tested on their ability to identify meanings of Māori words in a forced-choice definition task, and they did this relatively well. Then, words with low accuracy were selected for Experiment 2, where non-Māori-speaking New Zealanders and non-New Zealanders were asked to learn meanings for Māori words and nonwords. New Zealanders performed better, indicating that familiarity with Māori word shapes confers an advantage. However, they showed no greater advantage for real words over nonwords. If these words are definitely in the proto-lexicon, then this would suggest that knowledge of individual word-forms does not, in fact, confer an advantage.

The Decline and Revival of Indigenous Tongues

explanation.text: 글의 대상은 말하지 못하지만 노출만으로 지식이 쌓인 사람들이다 — "New Zealanders who do not speak Maori but are regularly exposed to the language develop implicit knowledge of it". 그래서 ③이 제목이다. ①은 정규 교육을 다루는데 글은 그것을 비교 대상으로만 언급하고, ②④⑤는 소재가 인접할 뿐이다.

items.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.passage: Birds (Aves) are a group of animals with backbones. Birds are the only dinosaurs that survived the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction, and are part of the theropod group of dinosaurs. The word for "bird-like" is avian, from Latin language avis, bird. Birds are warm blooded. Their feathers help prevent loss of body heat. Modern birds do not have teeth. They have beaked jaws. Birds lay hard-shelled eggs. They have a high metabolic rate and a strong but lightweight skeleton. Their hearts have four chambers. Birds live all over the world. They range in size from the 5 cm (2 in) bee hummingbird to the 2.70 m (9 ft) ostrich. There are about ten thousand species of birds. More than half of these are passerines, or perching birds. Birds have wings. The wings develop differently in different species. The only known groups of birds without wings are the extinct moa and the elephant birds. Wings evolved from the forelimbs of birds. They give birds the ability to fly. Over time, many groups of birds evolved with smaller wings. These include ratites, penguins and many island species of birds. The digestive and respiratory systems of birds are also ____.
choices: shaped by the demands of flight
simplified by the loss of teeth
unusual among warm-blooded animals
inherited from theropod dinosaurs
linked to their great range of size

explanation.text: 마지막 문장의 "also" 는 앞서 나온 기준을 이어받는 표시인데, 그 기준은 "a strong but lightweight skeleton", "a high metabolic rate", 그리고 날개가 "give birds the ability to fly" 로 이어지는 비행이다. 그러므로 ① 이 정답이다. ② 의 이빨 없음과 ③ 의 온혈성은 지문에 나오지만 소화계·호흡계를 설명하는 기준이 아니고, ④ 의 수각류 계통은 기원을 말할 뿐 구조의 이유가 되지 못한다. ⑤ 의 크기 편차는 벌새와 타조를 든 대목의 소재일 뿐 두 기관과 연결되지 않는다.

items.stem: 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
items.passage:
Ines had never ventured beyond her own district until the autumn she turned nineteen. Her cousin Talia, four years older and benevolent in a fussy way, bought the ticket. The night coach waited beyond the fishery gate at the end of a brick corridor. Talia turned up her collar and pressed a folded map into her hand. Ines nodded without absorbing a word, because she was counting the coins in her coat. She watched Talia dwindle behind the glass, and then the town was gone.

Twice before dawn the coach stopped, and each time Ines woke aboard in the dark. She had folded the map so tightly that the road names had fractured apart. At the second stop a plump woman with a shrill accent asked where she was going. Ines said the coast, though she did not know how far it still lay. She thought of Talia, and of how quickly she would have asked the driver. Talia would have handled it with diplomacy, and indeed her voice would not have shaken.

Talia walked home past the leafless market square under a leaky wooden shelter. In her coat pocket she found the small brass key that Ines had forgotten. It opened the cottage they had never once abandoned in ten summers. Talia turned back at once, furious with herself, but the coach had departed. She wrote a letter instead and left it on the counter for the post. In it she promised to keep the key until Ines came for it herself.

Ines reached the coast a day late, and her spirits had begun to plummet. The letter was waiting at a homely boarding house, sodden and unopened. She read it twice on the step, and then briefly once more aloud. Talia had written nothing about the fare or the inconvenience she had caused. She had written only that the cottage door would stay shut until August. Ines put the letter where the coins had been and felt her own independence settle.
choices: Talia turned up her collar
she would have asked the driver
her voice would not have shaken
she was counting the coins
She wrote a letter instead

explanation.text: ①②③⑤는 모두 Talia 를 가리킨다 — "Talia turned up her collar and pressed a folded map into her hand"(①) · "She thought of Talia, and of how quickly she would have asked the driver"(②) · "Talia would have handled it with diplomacy, and indeed her voice would not have shaken"(③) · "She wrote a letter instead and left it on the counter for the post"(⑤, 앞 문장의 주어가 Talia 다). ④만 Ines 다 — "Ines nodded without absorbing a word, because she was counting the coins in her coat" 로, 고개를 끄덕인 사람과 동전을 세는 사람이 같다. 그래서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은 ④다.

items.source: The Night Coach to the Coast

items.passage: SEC. II.--OF THE DIFFERENT ACCOUNTS WHICH HAVE BEEN GIVEN OF THE NATURE OF VIRTUE. INTRODUCTION. The different accounts which have been given of the nature of virtue, or of the temper of mind which constitutes the excellent and praise-worthy character, may be reduced to three different classes. According to some, the virtuous temper of mind does not consist in any one species of affections, but in the proper government and direction of all our affections, which may be either virtuous or vicious according to the objects which they pursue, and the degree of vehemence with which they pursue them. According to these authors, therefore, virtue consists in propriety. According to others, virtue consists in the judicious pursuit of our own private interest and happiness, or in the proper government and direction of those selfish affections which aim solely at this end. In the opinion of these, therefore, virtue consists in prudence. Another set of authors make virtue consist in those affections only which aim at the happiness of others, not in those which aim at our own. According to them, therefore, disinterested benevolence is the only motive which can stamp upon actions the character of virtue.
choices: 사려가 덕의 전부라는 견해를 근거를 들어 옹호하려고

남을 위하는 마음만이 참된 덕임을 증명해 보이려고
덕이라는 말이 언제부터 쓰였는지 그 유래를 캐 보려고

explanation.text: ②가 글의 목적이다. 첫 문단이 "may be reduced to three different classes" 라 선언하고, 뒤가 propriety · prudence · benevolence 셋을 차례로 갈라 놓는다. 나머지는 목적이 아니다: ①과 ④는 그 셋 가운데 하나를 글 전체의 주장으로 오해한 것이고, ③의 수양 방법과 ⑤의 낱말 유래는 글에 없다.

items.passage: Researchers have identified a widely found gene in plants as a key transporter of a hormone that influences the size of corn. The discovery offers plant breeders a new tool to develop desirable dwarf varieties that could enhance the crop’s resilience and profitability. A team of scientists spent years working to pinpoint the functions of the gene ZmPILS6. Now, they have been able to characterize it as an important driver of plant size and architecture, a carrier for an auxin hormone that helps govern growth in roots below ground and shoots, or stalks, above ground. Their findings are published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. “A hallmark of the current age of science is that we have all this high-quality genome data, whether for corn or humans or other organisms, and now we have the task of figuring out what the genes actually do,” says Dior Kelley, assistant professor of genetics, development and cell biology at Iowa State University, who led the research team. The group used “reverse genetic screening” (from the gene to traits expressed in the plant), combined with other techniques, as they tracked their gene’s role in corn development.
choices: 옥수수는 키가 작은 품종으로 모두 바꾸어 심어야 한다

explanation.text: 필자가 독자에게 요구하는 것은 연구 책임자의 말에 담겨 있다 — "we have all this high-quality genome data … and now we have the task of figuring out what the genes actually do". ③이다. ① 은 발견의 쓰임(왜성 품종)을 당위로 부풀린 것이고, ④ 는 글이 뿌리와 줄기를 함께 든 것을 좁혔다. ②·⑤ 는 글에 없다.

Feudal institutions awakened a lively sympathy for the sufferings of certain men, but none at all for the miseries of mankind. They infused generosity rather than mildness into the manners of the time, and although they prompted men to great acts of self-devotion, they engendered no real sympathies; for real sympathies can only exist between those who are alike; and in aristocratic ages men acknowledge none but the members of their own caste to be like themselves. When the chroniclers of the Middle Ages, who all belonged to the aristocracy by birth or education, relate the tragical end of a noble, their grief flows apace; whereas they tell you at a breath, and without wincing, of massacres and tortures inflicted on the common sort of people. Not that these writers felt habitual hatred or systematic disdain for the people; war between the several classes of the community was not yet declared.
